key_insight: A flow-based machine-learned probability distribution can closely approximate the natural invariant distribution of turbulent channel flow, enabling realistic synthetic turbulence generation and flow reconstruction.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to generate physically consistent turbulent fields for simulation initialization, reduced-cost uncertainty studies, and data-driven reconstruction from sparse observations.
method: Train a flow-based generative model on a minimal conditional flow unit for channel flow at Re_τ = 180.
Sample both unconditional and conditional turbulent fields using a consistent conditional sampling procedure.
Check physical ensemble statistics, conditional consistency, and dynamical invariance against direct numerical simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with direct numerical simulation in key statistics and dynamics, including intermittency, nonlinear energy transfer, and stationary ensemble behavior when learned fields are used as DNS initial conditions.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated for turbulent channel flow at Re_τ = 180, so generalization to other Reynolds numbers, geometries, or higher-dimensional flows still needs validation.
paper_title: A machine-learned probability distribution in the phase space of turbulent channel flow for synthetic turbulence and flow reconstruction
